name: AI incidents & governance
summary: The European Commission confirmed on 19 Nov that a cyberattack on its internal systems used AI tools
state: A European Commission spokesperson confirmed on 19 Nov that a cyberattack first detected on 22 Oct was carried out with AI tools, the first such case the EU has reported; several internal applications were taken down and most have been restored (CP24, citing AP; The Star). No attribution has been made. Searches on 25 Nov found no newer major AI misuse incident, no AI-enabled attack on critical infrastructure and no mass harm event, so Watch holds.
for_you: Little direct effect on most people. The NCSC publishes guidance for organisations on AI-enabled cyber threats and on phishing and deepfake scams.
rubric_hit: Watch: significant AI misuse incident (AI-assisted attack on the European Commission, confirmed 19 Nov); no attack on critical infrastructure

sources.title: CP24 — A cyberattack using artificial intelligence targeted the EU in October, official says
The Star — EU Commission confirms it was targeted in cyberattack through use of AI tools

why: Powerful AI systems are being deployed faster than safeguards; serious incidents or governance breakdowns carry systemic risk.
drivers: Model releases, misuse incidents, regulation, compute controls, deepfakes in elections.

rubric.alert: AI-enabled attack on critical infrastructure, or AI-attributed mass harm event.
rubric.watch: A significant AI misuse incident, major deepfake disruption, or regulatory confrontation.
rubric.normal: No serious AI-attributed harm events or governance shocks this week.
